status_reason: The survey is every two years and the consistent 2017-2023 analytic file gives only 4 points (2017, 2019, 2021, 2023); the 2025 wave is not released yet. Too short for the five-year baseline and ten-year swing.
name: Adults who volunteered
definition: Share of people 16 and older in the New York metro area who volunteered through or for an organization in the previous 12 months (formal volunteering), from the Current Population Survey Civic Engagement and Volunteering Supplement.

source.name: AmeriCorps and U.S. Census Bureau, Current Population Survey Civic Engagement and Volunteering Supplement, 2017-2023 stacked analytic file (data.americorps.gov be5g-4c5r)

peers.note: Metro areas, not cities. AmeriCorps says the CEV supports reliable estimates only for the 12 largest metro areas, so only peers whose metro is among them are shown (Dallas and Fort Worth share one metro). Rates computed from the same microdata with the same weights as the New York figure.

source.name: AmeriCorps and Census Bureau, CPS Civic Engagement and Volunteering Supplement 2017-2023 stacked analytic file

values.geo_name: New York-Newark-Jersey City, NY-NJ-PA Metro Area
Los Angeles-Long Beach-Anaheim, CA Metro Area
Houston-The Woodlands-Sugar Land, TX Metro Area

method: Computed from AmeriCorps' CEV analytic microdata: weighted share of respondents (ages 16+) with volunteer = 1, using the supplement weight supwgt, among respondents with a non-missing volunteer answer and positive weight, for the New York-Newark-Jersey City metro area (topmsa = 1). The same calculation reproduces AmeriCorps' published national rates (2017 30.3, 2019 30.0, 2021 23.2, 2023 28.3) and New York State rates, which the script checks. Unweighted NY metro respondents: 2017: 2666, 2019: 2217, 2021: 1763, 2023: 1713.
caveats: The geography is the 2020-definition New York metro area (including northern New Jersey, the lower Hudson Valley and Long Island), not the five boroughs; the CEV is not designed for city-level estimates.
Survey estimates with sampling error; margins of error are not published for metro rates and are not computed here (no replicate weights in the file).
The survey runs every two years; the September 2025 wave is scheduled for public release on 1 December 2026, after this was fetched.
2021 was collected during the pandemic and is low everywhere.
